name: Neonode N1
pros: Dedicated rear camera for quick snapshot captures
Li-Ion 1100 mAh battery offers solid operating endurance for daily use
Expandable memory via SD/MMC, up to 1 GB, 64 MB included
cons: No official IP rating for dust or water resistance
Standard charging speeds without ultra-fast charging support

reviews.title: Solid performance for its 2003 launch era
reviews.body: Picking this up around its release period, the Microsoft Windows CE.NET experience felt snappy and responsive for the price tier. The VGA camera delivered reliable shots in outdoor lighting.

reviews.title: Reliable battery and daily usability
reviews.body: The Li-Ion 1100 mAh power cell paired with Neonode's software tuning easily lasted through a full work day with mixed web browsing, calls, and media playback.

reviews.title: Refined hardware styling and build
reviews.body: The physical chassis of the Neonode N1 feels well-balanced in hand. Its 88 x 52 x 21 mm (3.46 x 2.05 x 0.83 in) make it easy to hold during long daily sessions.

reviews.title: Great value for the hardware specifications
reviews.body: For the price point, getting standard platform performance alongside 16MB RAM storage, SD/MMC slot made the Neonode N1 an easy recommendation among rivals in 2003.

reviews.title: Smooth day-to-day software responsiveness
reviews.body: Operating on Microsoft Windows CE.NET, the user interface is intuitive with smooth system transitions. Core apps and browsing run without noticeable stutter.

reviews.title: Dependable display and audio clarity
reviews.body: The screen (Removable Li-Ion 1100 mAh battery, 2.2", 176x220 pixels) produces vibrant colors for video streaming, and call clarity through the earpiece is crystal clear.

reviews.title: A well-rounded package from Neonode
reviews.body: Overall, the Neonode N1 proved to be a durable and well-engineered mobile device representing Neonode's design philosophy nicely.
